breakpoints.code: ret = gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8(*key, &data, GNUTLS_X509_FMT_DER, password, type == GNUTLS_BAG_PKCS8_KEY ? GNUTLS_PKCS_PLAIN : 0);
breakpoints.note: By this point the PKCS#12 blob has been imported successfully, a key bag has been extracted, and its PKCS#8 bytes are dispatched into the private-key importer with the harness password `"1234"`, admitting the witness to the vulnerable GOST key path.
First project statement on the witnessed path that reads the attacker-controlled GOST curve OID from the PKCS#8 parameters into a parser buffer.

The staged patch adds a `NEED_GOSTDSA` capability check, renames the local curve accessors and objects to GC256B/GC512A names, and rewrites `get_supported_gost_curve()` so `GOST256CPA`, `GOST256CPXA`, and `GOST256B` all resolve via the `GOST256B` fallthrough to `nettle_get_gost_gc256b()`, while `GOST512A` resolves to `nettle_get_gost_gc512a()`. It also moves the local-only VKO and unmask declarations into `gostdsa2.h`, so this path no longer returns the old local `_gnutls_gost_256cpa` or `_gnutls_gost_512a` objects.
